Chapter Four: Open or Engaged.
You know, there’s something powerful about being around someone who’s truly open—someone who’s not just hearing you, but actually listening, and willing to share their own thoughts honestly.
Think back to a time when you felt safe enough to say exactly what was on your mind. Maybe it was with a close friend, or even a colleague who just gets it. The conversation felt easy, right? That’s what it means to be open and engaged.
It’s not just about nodding along or waiting for your turn to speak. It’s about showing that you care, asking real questions, and sometimes sharing a little bit of yourself in return. When that happens, people can sense it—and trust starts to build.
So, how do you spot someone who’s open and engaged? Watch for the way they make eye contact, the way they ask follow-up questions, or how they actually remember what you said last time. It’s in those little moments that real connection grows.
Here’s something to try: next time you’re in a conversation, notice if you’re really present, or if your mind’s wandering. What if you could be just a bit more open—maybe share something honest, or listen without planning your response? You might be surprised by how much deeper the conversation gets.
So, the next time you want to build trust or connect with someone, remember—it all starts with being open and engaged. Sometimes, that’s all it takes for a good conversation to turn into a great one.
